description: This updated edition of the best-selling Small Engines and Power Equipment is more than a simple engine repair manual. Designed for the beginner with little or no mechanical experience, this book is a graphically appealing, step-by-step guide that covers all of the most important engine maintenance and repair skills you'll need to keep your equipment running at peak performance. It also shows exactly how to perform mechanical upkeep and repairs on the most common outdoor power implements. With new and improved content for today's motorized equipment, this DIY bible includes engine and mechanical repair plus maintenance instruction for all your outdoor power equipment , including lawn mowers, snow blowers, chain saws, power washers, generators, leaf blowers, rototillers, wood splitters, lawn edgers, and weed whips. With clear how-to photos and detailed diagrams , you'll see exactly what needs to be done. A comprehensive troubleshooting guide helps you define problems and enact solutions. Among the many skills you'll learn are seasonal tune-ups, changing oil, servicing spark plugs, cleaning filters, replacing muffler, servicing the fuel tank, overhauling the carburetor, servicing brakes, inspecting flywheels, replacing the fuel pump, and replacing a rewind cord. With Small Engines and Outdoor Power Equipment 2nd Edition in your library, you won't need to haul the lawn mower off to the repair center and wait a few weeks just because a filter is plugged or the old gas needs to be replaced. description: Find the fault first. Then fix it. An engine that will not start can have a dozen causes. This book shows a beginner how to narrow it down with a ten-minute walk-around and four simple tests : spark, compression, fuel and plug reading. Each result tells you the next step, so you stop guessing and stop buying parts you do not need. Then it walks you through ten illustrated repairs , from the spark plug to the muffler, each starting with safety and ending with how you know it worked. What you get A walk-around and four tests for four-stroke mower, generator, snowblower and pressure washer engines A flowchart for no-start, rough running and weak power, with every path ending at a named repair Ten illustrated repairs: spark plug, air filter, fuel system, float carburetor, diaphragm carburetor, ignition checks, valve, governor and throttle linkage (check only), oil and cooling, muffler and spark arrester A chapter on two-stroke handhelds such as trimmers, blowers and small chainsaws, limited to fuel and carburetor basics Safety rules for fuel, fire, hot parts, spring tension and carbon monoxide Seasonal maintenance and storage, plus a repair-or-replace decision table A guide to when to stop and take the machine to a shop Four worked case files, a symptom index, a glossary and a one-page bench card Numbers you can trust Every number in the book comes from a maker document named beside it. Where there is no source, the book does not invent one: it sends you to your own engine manual, which always comes first. Who it is for First-time owners of lawn mowers, generators, snowblowers and pressure washers who want to understand what their engine is doing and fix the simple problems themselves. title: The Illustrated Small Engine Repair Handbook: Step-by-Step Troubleshooting, Repair & Maint
description: Find the next useful test and follow a clear repair process without scattered instructions or parts guesswork. Does your engine crank without starting, run briefly and stop, or lose power when the work begins? Have you cleaned or replaced a part and still been left with the same symptom? Do you want illustrated steps that help you inspect, test, service, and check your equipment with a clear purpose? Different faults can produce similar symptoms. A wet spark plug, an unstable idle, or a low compression reading needs a method and context before it can support a repair decision. Disconnected tips rarely show how those observations fit together. Start with what the machine does, then follow the evidence through the job. The Illustrated Small Engine Repair Handbook combines symptom charts, representative component illustrations, numbered workshop procedures, and checks after the repair. It covers common single-cylinder gasoline engines used in lawn mowers, generators, chainsaws, trimmers, snowblowers, and other outdoor power equipment. Build a repair process you can use at the workbench. Symptom-based troubleshooting : follow routes for no rotation, no start, starting and stopping, surging, smoke, hot failure, vibration, and failed stopping controls. Illustrated fuel and carburetor service : distinguish metal float-bowl, plastic modular, and diaphragm designs, record hoses and linkage, and check sealing before returning to use. Ignition and starting procedures : work through spark testing, stop circuits, spark plugs, flywheel inspection, recoil starting, and low-voltage electric-start checks. title: How a Small Engine Works for Beginners: Engine Basics, Maintenance, and Troubleshooting Ex
description: How a Small Engine Works A Clear Guide to Understanding Small Engines and Why They Fail Small engines power the equipment people rely on every day. Lawn mowers, snowblowers, generators, pressure washers, pumps, and utility machines all depend on compact engines designed to deliver reliable power with very few parts. Yet when these engines run poorly or fail, the cause often feels confusing and unpredictable. This book explains what is actually happening inside a small engine, using clear language and real-world examples. It focuses on how fuel, air, ignition, compression, lubrication, cooling, and load interact in simple mechanical systems and why small engines react so quickly when something is wrong. This book teaches understanding. It shows how to read engine behavior, recognize symptoms, and trace problems back to the system involved. Surging, stalling under load, hard starting, overheating, backfiring, and sudden failures are explained logically instead of treated as mysteries. Inside this book you will learn: • How small engines convert fuel into usable motion • Why small engines stall instead of powering through resistance • The real differences between two-stroke and four-stroke engines • How carburetors, governors, and ignition systems actually work • Why air cooling and cleanliness matter so much • How load, shaft orientation, and equipment design affect behavior • How to diagnose problems by symptom rather than guessing • What mistakes commonly shorten engine life This book is written for equipment owners, DIY-minded readers, and anyone who wants a solid understanding of how small engines work. description: Your mower won't start. Your generator keeps dying. You don't know if it's fuel, spark, or something worse — and you're tired of guessing. Most repair books force you to learn engine anatomy before you can find your answer. They're organized by system — fuel, ignition, compression — when what you actually have is a symptom . This book fixes that. Small Engine Diagnosis is organized the way you actually experience problems: by what's happening, not by what's inside. Won't start. Starts then dies. Runs rough. Smokes. Leaks. Loses power. Flip to your symptom, follow the decision tree, and get a specific answer — not a shrug and a list of five equally likely guesses. What makes this different: The Engine Profile Filter — a one-time, 10-minute setup that narrows every diagnosis to your specific engine (2-stroke or 4-stroke, carbureted or fuel-injected, and more), instead of generic advice that half-applies to your machine Symptom-first navigation — no need to understand engine systems before you start; just find what you're seeing and go Every decision tree ends somewhere specific — a real fix, or a clear "this needs a professional" — never an unhelpful list of maybes Color-coded smoke diagnosis, leak-location trees, and a Repair-or-Replace framework so you stop wasting money on the wrong parts Covers: mowers, generators, snowblowers, trimmers, pressure washers, and chainsaws. Whether you're a homeowner trying to avoid another repair shop bill, an off-grid or rural reader who needs equipment working now , or someone flipping used small engines and needs to diagnose before you buy — this book gets you from symptom to solution fast.
